📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is part of a forthcoming patch that adds new high-visibility options.

Google Maps is getting new high-visibility options, according to a report by Android Authority. This should make the maps easier to see under certain real-world lighting conditions, due to updated color palettes in both the light and dark modes.

Sources indicate that for instance, the dark mode looks darker than ever before. It features blacker backgrounds and a purple navigation route. Bodies of water and green spaces are both darker, making them easier to identify at a glance.

It has been revealed that the updated light mode also features some noticeable changes. Green spaces are darker and a bit more muted. Off-white and beige sections have changed to different shades of gray, while the blue location indicator has turned purple. The end result is a slightly more subdued look.

1️⃣ FIRST LOOK: Google Maps could soon look very different while you're navigating🚨.

We've managed to unlock a latest setting hidden in the latest version of Google Maps, and it gives navigation a completely different color scheme. Here's what we found🧵 pic.twitter.com/K7sOtGxLdS.

— Android Authority (@AndroidAuth) November 24, 2026.

Industry observers note that beyond new color palettes, the navigation experience looks unchanged. It still offers turn-by-turn direction indicators and the bottom information panel remains the same across the two new styles.

These settings aren't publicly available yet. Android Authority managed to enable them via the latest Google Maps version, which lets users swap between the standard old-school palette and these upcoming high-visibility options. We don't know when the update will go live. Engadget has reached out to Google to ask about a timeframe and will update this post when we hear back.

According to recent reports, this is just the latest nifty feature coming to Google Maps. The platform recently introduced 3D navigation maps and is stuffing chatbot functionality just about everywhere.

#81593. Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (783 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (783 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era.
  • “Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch.
  • Sources indicate that it’s been a bumpy road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year.

“Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.”.

Sources indicate that it’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants, but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster.

That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market.

“Global capacity of natural gas is only about 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, where solar is already at well over a terawatt,” he said. “Probably the most notable lesson that we’ve learned over the last 20 years of backing companies is that Wright’s Law is the thing you want to leverage — making the same thing over and over again.”.

Both solar and most forms of long-duration energy storage are built on small, modular technologies that can be manufactured at massive scale. “This is about speed and scale and economics, and we can win across all those dimensions,” Porter noted.

G2VP had an early window into AI data center development, having led Crusoe’s Series C. “We’ve had a front-row seat at what’s been happening at that organization, how they’ve evolved, how the different waves of data centers have evolved,” Porter remarked.

In a recent development, the venture firm estimates that data center investment will top $4 trillion until the end of the decade. As the next wave takes shape, the firm sees two different paths for data centers: small, on-grid facilities with their own generating capacity, and larger data centers powered by solar and long-duration energy storage.

“The massive idea is to go off-grid,” Porter said. “What that would enable you to do is build with renewables in a way that’s independent of the grid. You can determine your own fate, go around some of the constraints of permitting, whether that’s access to the grid or air permits. You can accelerate your time to market dramatically.”.

In recent years, energy storage has been synonymous with lithium-ion batteries, which are too expensive to compete with fossil fuels for round-the-clock power. But a newly introduced generation of long-duration energy storage products from the likes of Form Energy and G2VP portfolio organization Antora Energy have brought the cost per megawatt-hour down significantly.

Even though the technologies might be a few years away from broad acceptance among data center developers, Porter said they should start thinking about them now.

“It’s analogous to surfing the biggest waves off of Mavericks here in Northern California. The wave is so massive that you really have to be paddling and moving and be incredibly nimble to catch it. If you’re at a standstill, it’s just gonna blow you by,” he mentioned.

#81591. Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (502 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A group of South Africans returned from the war in Ukraine earlier this year.
  • A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.
  • The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of South Africans returned from the war in Ukraine earlier this year.

A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.

The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars.

Twenty-four-year-old Wesley Sothole, who pleaded guilty, was handed a five-year suspended prison sentence and was ordered to be deported from South Africa.

He is one of five Zimbabweans who were arrested at OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg on 8 November. South African prosecutors have not confirmed which side the Zimbabweans allegedly intended to fight for.

Sothole's four co-accused have yet to enter pleas and are due to return to the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on 1 December for further plea and sentencing proceedings.

Another four Zimbabweans were arrested at a hotel in Johannesburg at the same time in a joint operation and are facing a different court process.

The investigation has involved South African police, Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies.

South Africa's Foreign Military Assistance Act was passed in 1998 at a time when the government was concerned about members of the former apartheid security services going to fight elsewhere in Africa.

There has been growing concern across Africa over the recruitment of its citizens to fight in the war in Ukraine, with some reportedly being lured to Russia by promises of lucrative civilian employment.

A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia.

Some have been captured and are being held as prisoners of war.

In March, Kenya estimated that 252 of its citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia.

Sources indicate that kenyan Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the matter. He mentioned an agreement had been reached for Russia to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals.

In the same month, Zimbabwe stated that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines.

The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 of its nationals who were allegedly tricked into joining the war.

In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war.

South Africa's government said it condemned "the exploitation of young vulnerable people by individuals working with foreign military entities".

Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa.

Additional reporting by Khanyisile Ngcobo in Johannesburg.

#81587. Wireless Android Auto has a phone battery draining problem, but you can fix it

📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Wireless Android Auto has a phone battery draining problem, but you can fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A vent mount and a few settings changes are enough to block the drain.
  • An hour of wireless Android Auto can sap up to 16 percent of a phone's battery when you've got everything turned on.
  • After all, wireless Android Auto uses both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and both stay switched on for your entire drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A vent mount and a few settings changes are enough to block the drain.

An hour of wireless Android Auto can sap up to 16 percent of a phone's battery when you've got everything turned on. Navigation, as well as music, can heat your phone up, which isn't great news since most people will charge their phones during the drive. That charging adds even more heat, and a phone that gets too hot may slow down its own charging to protect the battery.

After all, wireless Android Auto uses both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and both stay switched on for your entire drive. Long stints using navigation and other demanding apps while charging have been acknowledged as some of the reasons a Pixel can overheat. Once it's too hot, the phone might reduce processor performance or partly switch off mobile data, including 5G.

In a recent development, but there are a few things you can do to help mitigate battery drain and heat, like turning off 5G or using offline maps. And for longer drives, you can plug the phone in to maintain its charge and keep it out of direct sunlight, ideally near an air-conditioning vent to help it stay cool.

Google has remarked that managing heat was one of the main reasons it capped the Pixel 10 and Pixel 10 Pro at 15W wireless charging, because a wireless pad can add even more thermal energy. A phone that's sitting on a pad, which itself is probably on a sunny dashboard while running navigation, can build up heat from several sources at once, potentially slowing charging.

Google's advice to prevent a Pixel from overheating is to keep it out of direct sunlight and away from hot vehicles and poorly ventilated spots. One way to reduce heat is to use a vent mount while the vent is blowing cold air instead of a dashboard cradle in full sun. Even moving the phone somewhere with ample airflow while not relying on charging during wireless Android Auto use can help substantially.

A USB connection can generally keep your phone cooler and charge it more effectively than wireless Android Auto on a wireless charging mount. But car ports vary, and some vehicle USB ports could be too slow to stop the battery from draining, depending on automaker specifications. If you want to switch to a wired connection, Android Auto has a developer menu you can access in seconds. While Google removed the wireless Android Auto switch from the app's regular settings in version 8.7, it remains available in the hidden developer settings, so you can turn wireless Android Auto off and connect the phone with a USB cable.

Industry observers note that switching from 5G to LTE appears to make the biggest difference to battery life, because some networks force a phone to maintain an LTE connection alongside 5G, which increases power consumption. LTE is thankfully fast enough for navigation and music. To improve your Samsung Galaxy's battery performance, go to Settings > Connections > Mobile networks > Network mode and select LTE preferred. On other phones, look for Network mode or Preferred network type. Turning off 3D buildings in Google Maps can also help to reduce heat. With your car parked, open Google Maps on the car's screen, go into its Settings and turn off 3D buildings.

According to recent reports, google Maps can save a map of your route before you leave, reducing mobile data use and strain on the device. Tap your profile picture, then Offline maps > Select your own map, adjust the area to cover your route and tap Download. Offline maps can't reroute around live traffic or new road complications as they develop, so going offline is generally best saved for long, predictable drives such as those on a highway or where you're familiar with the roads.

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning help apps get better location information, too. You can switch both off under Settings > Location > Location services, removing another background job. Wireless Android Auto still needs Wi-Fi and Bluetooth turned on, though. To stop it launching when you don't want it to, you can toggle off the setting Start Android Auto while locked, which can prevent it from starting while your phone is locked. This doesn't stop calls from connecting over Bluetooth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed the companies to pull the human safety driver from behind the wheel.

The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027.

The milestone comes just 16 months after Uber revealed an ambitious plan to launch a premium robotaxi service using Lucid electric vehicles outfitted with autonomous vehicle technology developed by startup Nuro.

Recent findings suggest that that plan came with hefty investments in both companies and much-needed endorsements of their respective products. Uber initially agreed to invest $300 million in Lucid — a figure that has since ballooned to $500 million. Uber also agreed to invest nearly $500 million in Nuro, TechCrunch previously reported, citing sources familiar with the deal.

Sources indicate that the agreement provided both Lucid and Nuro with boosts beyond the obvious capital injection. Uber agreed to buy at least 20,000 of Lucid Gravity SUVs over the next six years, giving the struggling EV maker a more predictable source of revenue. Nuro, meanwhile, was less than a year removed from announcing a risky, but necessary pivot away from developing driverless delivery vehicles and toward licensing its autonomous vehicle technology to automakers and mobility companies.

Nuro has spent nearly a year testing the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with a human safety operator behind the wheel. The California Department of Motor Vehicles, the agency that regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, granted Nuro a driverless AV permit in May 2026.

Uber and Nuro are also testing autonomous vehicles on public roads in Houston with human safety operators behind the wheel. Nuro is supplementing that on-road testing with closed-course testing and simulation to validate the self-driving system before opening the robotaxis to the public. The companies’ combined engineering fleet of autonomous vehicles, which stood at 100 AVs earlier this year, is expanding as Lucid begins manufacturing the first production versions of the robotaxis at its Arizona factory.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi, unveiled in January 2026, is outfitted with high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar sensors, and radars that help the self-driving system perceive the real-world environment and operate in it. Uber, which will own and operate the fleet, has focused its efforts on the in-cabin experience, including how riders will interact with the vehicle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The app will prompt people to use the agent to sort through their saved content.

When I first tried out Meta's personal agent Muse, I found that one of the more useful tasks it could perform was asking it to organize all the videos and posts I've saved on Instagram over the years. Now, Meta is bringing that functionality into the Instagram app itself.

According to recent reports, the tech giant is integrating Muse directly into Instagram and will begin prompting people to use the agent when they save posts. Muse is also getting its own presence in Instagram DMs so users can start chats with the assistant inspired by the content they're seeing.

It has been revealed that the fresh features will be available to people who have connected their Instagram and Muse accounts. And Instagram owners in the United States will begin to see prominent pop-ups suggesting they use Muse to organize their saved content in specific collections, like recipe videos or travel clips.

It's a familiar move from Meta's growth-hacking playbook. When the firm was growing Threads, it began pushing popular posts from the app to the top of Facebook and Instagram feeds. Today, Threads has more than 500 million people. Now the company is likely hoping the in-app nudges will draw more Instagram users to Muse, which passed 10 million users last month. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently stated that he wants Muse to one day reach billions of people and has predicted that it could one day generate more revenue for the company than its existing suite of apps.

The push could also be somewhat confusing for owners. Instagram still has a separate Meta AI chatbot that users can DM with. That bot, which is meant to be more of a generic AI that can answer questions, isn't going away according to an Instagram spokesperson. Muse in DMs, on the other hand, is meant to be more of an assistant-like experience. For example, you can send it travel content you want it to research for an upcoming vacation. You can also ask for it to shop for specific items or check on your other DM threads.

According to recent reports, muse in Instagram will still be more limited than the actual Muse app or web interface, though. While you can send it to-dos or have it track Instagram-specific tasks, you'll probably still need to use the Muse app or website to see what it does with all your Instagram messages.

GisÃ¨le Pelicot has said she has been "once again humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media to promote a book about coercive control.

The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay.

Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious.

The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".

Pelicot told BFM: "I am deeply shocked that images from the most intimate part of my private life are being displayed and exploited for commercial purposes.".

"Today I find myself once again humiliated, exposed and hurt, as if the ordeal of the trial had not been enough," she remarked.

The essay was written by Sabine Prokhoris, a philosopher and psychoanalyst, who has previously criticised the Me Too movement.

French media reported that Tinbad, a small Paris publishing house, emailed nude photos of Pelicot taken by her ex-husband to some media outlets in order to promote the essay.

In a statement on its website, Tinbad said that no further print runs of the book would be produced beyond the 280 copies already in circulation.

"We offer our sincerest apologies to Ms GisÃ¨le Pelicot," it said. The company also apologised to the author.

Tinbad remarked "no images of rape or pornographic videos" were sent to the media.

French news agency AFP quoted the blurb of the book as saying coercive control was "a cornerstone of #MeToo orthodoxy".

"These psychological situations, fundamentally ambiguous in nature, involve each of the parties in an equally responsible, though not symmetrical, way," it said.

Pelicot's lawyer Christophe Bigot told BFM the book "calls into question her status as a victim".

Prokhoris told AFP that she placed "full responsibility" for the "inappropriate" promotional campaign on her publisher.

Fifty men were convicted alongside Pelicot's ex-husband in 2024, in a case that made her a global feminist icon.

After her husband was arrested for secretly filming underneath women's skirts in a supermarket, she discovered she had been repeatedly raped by dozens of men, including her husband, while unconscious, over a period of nearly a decade.

Pelicot said she decided to waive her right to anonymity to show how "shame has to change sides" from victims to perpetrators.

Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1392 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick noted Monday.
  • It has been revealed that it seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there.
  • Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick noted Monday.

It has been revealed that it seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved.

Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either.

According to recent reports, “This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick said. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.”.

Utah’s attorney general, Derek Brown, had filed both civil and criminal charges against Kalshi, as he defended the state’s 130-year ban on gambling.

In a recent development, in a press release discussing the initial lawsuit, he accused Kalshi of running “an online casino” that violates the state’s constitution. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution,” Brown mentioned. “For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”.

According to recent reports, late Monday, a major Utah-area news outlet, KSL.com, reported that Brown was prepared to jail Kalshi’s co-founders, who had been summoned to be booked on 14 charges on December 5. He defended those aims, saying, “There is a question I have seen from people asking, ‘Well, do we modify this booking process if someone is a very wealthy and well-known tech billionaire?’ and the answer is ‘No, the process is the process; we don’t modify it based on who you are.’”.

However, on Tuesday, Utah decided to drop the criminal charges against Kalshi, McGavick confirmed to Ars. In a statement on X, Kalshi general counsel Yaakov Roth stated, “We are pleased that Utah has chosen to dismiss criminal charges against Kalshi, while proceeding with civil litigation. Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized. We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.”.

In a press release, Brown explained that the charges were dropped specifically due to the pause.

“Kalshi said it would geofence Utah, which blocks access to its site in the state,” the press release said. “The tech giant also committed to monitor for Utah-based IP addresses trying to reach its site. The Office then reevaluated its position and moved to dismiss the criminal case against the company and the individual defendants.”.

Brown threatened that the charges would be raised again if Kalshi tried to renew operations.

It has been revealed that “Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown said. Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every company in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”.

Discussion of the Kalshi pause in a Utah sub-Reddit found some Redditors skeptical of the state’s cases as potentially overreaching.

However, many top commenters seemed pleased with the enforcement efforts, suggesting that Utah may have bipartisan support among some residents. One commenter cheered on the attorney general’s efforts as “the one item in the Utah GOP’s agenda I can get behind,” while another agreed that “prediction markets are incredibly toxic and are manipulated against ordinary people.”.

In a recent development, many complained that Kalshi ads flooded their social media feeds. Some suggested the state should focus on banning advertising of prediction markets, while potentially still allowing adults to trade on event contracts if they want to throw their “money away.”.

Fears of insider trading were also raised. One commenter laid out why prediction markets seem suspiciously designed to promote insider trading and other market manipulation:.

“I’m pretty libertarian and hate banning things. But gambling and prediction markets are a scourge. Even the term ‘prediction market’ is a misnomer. Because ultimately when people with big dollars get involved it creates a financial incentive for them to make fucked up things happen in the real world. Think about it, decades ago we understood that sports betting was a problem because it corrupted sports—something that ultimately is pretty meaningless. Then we got all these people betting on the stock market with puts and it created huge incentives to cause havoc with markets. Now if people are betting big money on politics and wars and everything else, it just means people with influence can make money by making improbable/unexpected things happen.”.

Recent findings suggest that one commenter joked, “I wonder how Kashi would have reacted if the judge in charge of their case had ‘traded’ $500,000 on the event of them losing the case. Not a problem at all, right?”.

On the same day Kalshi confirmed its temporary pause in Utah, a judge rejected a request from New York Attorney General Letitia James to immediately shut down Kalshi in that state, Courthouse News reported.

Latest York Supreme Court Justice Melissa Crane said she was “uncomfortable” granting the temporary restraining order so early in the case because “there does seem to be an indication that there would be market disruption that I’m concerned about.” Kalshi attorney Grant Mainland described it a little differently, claiming that a sudden halt would cause a “market emergency.”.

According to recent reports, “I think this is the ultimate relief in the case, which is improper for me to do without full briefing,” Crane said. Instead of granting James’ request, she recommended that Kalshi take steps to address the state’s top concerns by considering “safeguards for consumers between 18 and 20,” who are under the state’s legal gambling age, Courthouse News reported.

According to Kalshi’s estimates, New York’s Kalshi user base (1.5 million) is much larger than Utah’s, so the market disruption from the Utah shutdown may not have carried the same dire stakes for Kalshi or its broader user base.

Industry observers note that the CFTC has sought to intervene in that case, too, and it seems clear that Kalshi expects the questions of who can regulate prediction markets and what trading qualifies as a “bet” to reach the Supreme Court. Kalshi’s spokesperson did not respond to Ars’ questions on how the Utah pause broadly impacted users or the platform.

So far, “three federal appeals courts have ruled that states can regulate prediction markets, while a fourth found they cannot,” Courthouse News reported. But despite the current balance tipping toward allowing states to regulate prediction markets, Kalshi appears confident that the Supreme Court will resolve the disparate court rulings in its favor.

In a lawsuit filed by a disgruntled Kalshi user, Kalshi argued that it would waste lower courts’ time to continue litigating these cases and that no case should be resolved until the Supreme Court weighs in.

In that case, Kalshi user Scott Bright alleged that he lost more than $300,000 on sports bets that were technically illegal in Washington.

According to recent reports, according to Kalshi, all of Bright’s claims rest “on the premise that state gambling laws reach KalshiEX’s federally regulated exchange—the question now before the Supreme Court. Plaintiff puts the cart before the horse; Defendants ask only that the Court let that threshold question be resolved first.”.

The court has yet to address Kalshi’s request to stay the case, but Bright has argued that Kalshi is trying to “sideline a case governed by binding Ninth Circuit precedent so that they can wait for a Supreme Court decision that may never come.”.

Sources indicate that kalshi did not respond to Ars’ request for a statement on Bright’s lawsuit. In their court filing, they argued that “a stay will let the Supreme Court address an problem that could dispose of every claim, will not meaningfully harm Plaintiff, and will spare Defendants and the Court litigation under a framework that may soon be displaced.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform.
  • It has been revealed that tidal noted it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year.
  • Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata indicates they are made fully using AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The manufacturer said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.

It has been revealed that tidal noted it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.

Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata indicates they are made fully using AI.

The organization said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

Industry observers note that the move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services, mentioned that it will introduce a toggle to let customers filter out AI music. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this problem, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.

Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, remarked on X.

A few months ago, @Tidal tagged and demonetized all wholly AI-generated tracks to protect the authenticity of real artists. But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done….

The company remarked that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.

In a recent development, meanwhile, music labels are trying to make money by partnering with platforms and AI model makers to sell their catalog for training or remixing features. Goldman Sachs estimates that by 2035, AI-related licensing tools and fresh monetization opportunities have the potential to improve record labels’ revenue by 10%.

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Why your MacBook desktop Spaces keep rearranging themselves and how to stop it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disable a Mission Control-specific setting to keep Spaces from switching.
  • Sources indicate that in macOS, Spaces are virtual desktops that help organize and manage open apps and windows.
  • According to recent reports, while Spaces are particularly useful in organizing your desktop experience, their shortcomings become apparent when you notice their order changing in Mission Control as you switch between them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disable a Mission Control-specific setting to keep Spaces from switching.

Sources indicate that in macOS, Spaces are virtual desktops that help organize and manage open apps and windows. macOS allows up to 16 dedicated spaces for organizing your desktop. While fullscreen and split-mode apps also function like Spaces, they are different from numbered Spaces, particularly in how you access them using keyboard shortcuts.You can dedicate specific tasks to individual Spaces, such as communication, media consumption and web browsing. Another benefit to using Spaces is that they help consolidate open windows and prevent them from moving between virtual desktops when you switch Spaces.

According to recent reports, while Spaces are particularly useful in organizing your desktop experience, their shortcomings become apparent when you notice their order changing in Mission Control as you switch between them. This happens when you use the command + tab shortcut to switch Spaces, and macOS rearranges them depending on which Space was recently accessed. If you prefer having Spaces in an order of your choosing, the default auto-rearrangement feature can become frustrating.

However, the good news is that you don't have to be stuck with this feature forever. There's an option tucked away inside macOS' Settings app that prevents Spaces from rearranging themselves. Disabling it is all you need to make Spaces behave consistently on your MacBook or other macOS devices.

In a recent development, specifically, a toggle relevant to Mission Control is what causes Spaces to rearrange themselves on macOS, and it's enabled by default. To disable it, click the Apple icon in the menu bar and then click System Settings to open the Settings app. You can also use Spotlight search to look for System Settings.

While in the Settings app, click Desktop & Dock to bring up options specific to customizing your desktop experience. Scroll all the way to the bottom of these options to find the Mission Control section. Now, look for Automatically rearrange Spaces based on most recent use and disable it to stop Spaces from rearranging themselves.

That's it! You can now freely arrange and move between your Spaces without having to worry about macOS messing with them. Your Mac offers three options to navigate Spaces, including the three or four-finger trackpad swipe, Control + left/right arrow key shortcut and using the pointer to choose from available Spaces in Mission Control.

macOS offers several useful tools that, when combined, can help you get the most out of Spaces. For example, even though you cannot officially rename Spaces, they can still be assigned individual wallpapers for visual identity. You can do this by disabling the toggle to Show on all Spaces when changing wallpapers in a desktop Space.

Similarly, you can enable additional shortcuts besides those that let you switch between Spaces for a more control and precision. You can access these shortcuts from Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts > Mission Control > Mission Control drop-down menu. You'll see a list of shortcuts depending on the number of available Spaces, and you can enable individual shortcuts based on your requirements.

In a recent development, additionally, you can incorporate Hot Corners in your workflow for a more robust multitasking experience. Hot Corners allow you to assign specific functions to the four corners of your display, including an option to launch Mission Control. Since Spaces are inherently tied to Mission Control, the ability to flick the pointer to a corner and view all active Spaces at a glance can save valuable time.

According to recent reports, likewise, at times you might want to access an app from any Space, for example, Apple Music, to make music control simpler and more accessible. In such cases, Control + click the app in the dock > options > assign to All Desktop to make the chosen app persist across Spaces.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary.

In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.

"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions.

In the diary, written from 1992 to 2024, he also expresses regret over his 2018 visit to Chile, when he was criticised for defending a bishop who was accused of covering up sexual abuse committed by a priest.

Francis, who led the Catholic Church for 12 years until his death in 2025, later apologised and summoned the country's bishops to Rome, where they all offered to resign.

"Devastated because of the situation in Chile," Francis wrote in a 2021 entry.

"It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious.".

Of his encounters, which Francis interpreted as meetings with the devil, he stated he could not forget the devil's "menacing" eyes.

Industry observers note that "He looked at me with flaming eyes... more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire," he wrote of his second vision that he noted happened inside a Carmelite chapel while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires.

He mentioned the devil's presence intruded on his journeys, including during the visit to Chile amid the clerical sexual abuse scandal, and a meeting a few days after he had returned to Rome.

"I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".

The collection of diaries was edited by a longtime friend of Francis.

The late pope also revealed that while getting ready to go to sleep in June 2018, he "saw the gates of hell".

"I watched a little, and it terrified me," he stated, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".

"It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.

Cardinal Victor Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and friend of Francis, edited the diaries, which are the first by a pope to be released to the public since the 1960s.

Pope Francis was elected pope in 2013 and died aged 88 in April 2025.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Instagram consumers can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the organization unveiled on Tuesday.
  • The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.
  • Consumers can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Instagram consumers can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the organization unveiled on Tuesday. The social media network claims users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs.

The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content.

Consumers can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.

Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app.

Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore.

Meta also unveiled that owners can now do more with the posts and reels they’ve bookmarked on Instagram. For example, they can ask Muse to organize their saved content into custom folders, known as Collections. They could also ask Muse to turn a recipe video into a grocery list, turn the travel content from their favorite travel creators into an itinerary for an upcoming trip, or have Muse send them outfit ideas based on fashion reels they’ve collected.

Starting Tuesday, when users save a post on Instagram, they will see a prompt for Muse to organize it for them. This feature is launching in the U.S. and Canada.

Industry observers note that meta says that consumers remain in control of their Muse experience on Instagram. Nothing is shared, published, or sent without their approval, and they can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions at any time.

Hungary's fresh Prime Minister Peter Magyar arrived in Ukraine on Tuesday afternoon for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as well as with ethnic Hungarians living in the west of the country.

The meeting comes as both say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest — no doubt a welcome change for Kyiv after years of Viktor Orban obstructing funding for its self-defense against full-scaler Russian invasion.

Ukraine's Zelenskyy posted his thanks for the meeting with a photo on X, writing: "A visit that is sure to bring positive results. We already have agreements in the areas of politics, energy, and infrastructure. Thank you!".

The Ukrainian president noted agreements had been reached and teams had been tasked with implementing them.

Despite his softer approach, Magyar has said Hungary will not be sending arms to Kyiv while at the same time vowing, "we stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor.".

Magyar has insisted that the rights of tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians in the Transcarpathia — a region that was part of Austria-Hungary until the end of World War I and situated at the borders of Ukraine, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia — be resolved before Budapest can wholeheartedly back Ukraine and its possible accession to the European Union.

Relations deteriorated significantly over the glitch in 2017, when Kyiv passed a law making Ukrainian the official language of all secondary education in Ukraine, something Budapest viewed as discriminatory toward ethnic Hungarians.

Last month, Ukrainian lawmakers passed legislation allowing ethnic minorities in the country expanded rights regarding the teaching and use of their native languages. The move was welcomed by Budapest and Hungary dropped its opposition to Brussels opening accession talks with Ukraine.

Magyar pitched this week's trip — the first to Transcarpathia by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015 — in April, after defeating Orban.

It has been revealed that before departing for Ukraine, the Hungarian leader said: "I hope these talks will be successful. I think this is a historic day and a good opportunity to put Ukrainian-Hungarian relations on a new footing and to rebuild trust as we did with our other neighbors.".

Latest Update: How much does it cost to replace an out-of-warranty Tesla battery?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla battery can last for years beyond its warranty, but replacing it once that coverage runs out could cost you more than $20,000.
  • It has been revealed that being a Tesla owner sure makes you look cool and environmentally friendly, especially compared to your neighbor's gas-guzzling car.
  • How much you end up paying depends on your car's model and what other parts need repairing or swapping, but Tesla gives you no pricing chart to prepare for the expensive journey ahead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla battery can last for years beyond its warranty, but replacing it once that coverage runs out could cost you more than $20,000.

It has been revealed that being a Tesla owner sure makes you look cool and environmentally friendly, especially compared to your neighbor's gas-guzzling car. But all that excitement starts to fade when the EV doesn't go the distance it used to and a battery replacement feels like it's in the cards. Running a Tesla with an expired warranty can be nerve-racking, especially because a battery replacement could cost anywhere from about $12,600 to more than $20,000.

How much you end up paying depends on your car's model and what other parts need repairing or swapping, but Tesla gives you no pricing chart to prepare for the expensive journey ahead. The thing is, battery degradation is just basic chemistry, so losing a few miles of range as that EV gets older should not surprise you, even if you avoid the leading causes of EV battery damage. It isn't exactly a sign for you to worry about a full battery replacement either.

A 2025 report from Recurrent looked at over 30,000 EVs overall, and fewer than 4 percent had ever needed battery replacement, excluding major recalls of course. Recurrent used data from across several manufacturers and different model years, so it isn't exactly a Tesla-specific failure rate.

According to recent reports, while Tesla keeps its pricing under wraps, Earthling Automotive's 2025 pricing breakdown paints a pretty clear picture of how much you'd pay for a fresh EV battery. Keeping taxes aside, as they vary from state to state, you could end up shelling out anywhere between $12,600 and $13,350 with installation to replace the battery pack on an older rear-wheel-drive version of the Model 3.

That number shoots up to $17,250 for the all-wheel-drive (AWD) Model 3, and if you own a 2016-to-2021 Model S or Model X, you could be parting with about $19,500 to $20,500. But remember, Earthling's installation charges aren't Tesla Service rates, so your final bill could look a lot different based on things like battery configurations, labor charges and other replacement parts.

According to recent reports, in 2021, an invoice for a Model 3 battery replacement made the rounds online. The car had hit a large rock, so Tesla's warranty didn't cover the damage. The invoice listed a remanufactured battery at $13,500, and labor and add-ons brought the total to $16,550.67. If you'd rather not pay Tesla's prices, an independent EV specialist may be able to source a refurbished pack for cheap or repair specific faults, since an EV battery's life isn't always over once it's removed from your car. Still, your final bill depends on what's actually wrong with the battery, and it becomes a hard pill to swallow once it starts to match your aging Tesla's resale value.

Now, before you pull your hair out over signs that it's time to replace your EV battery, take your car in for a full diagnosis. Your best bet is getting Tesla to draw up an itemized bill, which will clearly show the battery cost (be it remanufactured or brand upcoming) along with labor and other add-ons.

Before you pay that bill, though, check whether your warranty already covers it, since Tesla's battery and drive unit warranty stays with you for eight years or 100,000, 120,000 or 150,000 miles, whichever comes first. The mileage limit depends directly on your EV's model and configuration, and Tesla promises at least 70 percent battery capacity retention while the warranty lasts. If your Tesla falls below that threshold, you could get a free repair or even a total battery replacement. If you somehow manage to wreck your battery or need a replacement after all, the new battery comes with a four-year or 50,000-mile parts warranty. And if for some reason Tesla swapped your battery for free under the original coverage, don't expect a fresh eight-year warranty period.

Even with all the support, if you're nervous about the most expensive part of your EV, send another $2,000 Tesla's way for the Battery Extended Service Agreement. You can get this for eligible Model 3 and Model Y cars before the original battery warranty runs out, and depending on what qualifies as a battery failure, you're covered with just a $500 service deductible. Mind you, this won't include regular wear and tear that every EV battery goes through over time. For the extra $2,000, you can add up to 24 months or 30,000 miles of added coverage to your old and faithful EV.

#81564. How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (919 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people.
  • Sources indicate that that’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews.
  • Sources indicate that as previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this “smoke taint” adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.

Sources indicate that that’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

Sources indicate that as previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018, OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper—identified the growing popularity of “dry hopping” (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.

It has been revealed that all beer contains hops, a key flavoring agent that also imparts useful antimicrobial properties. (Beer spoils quickly without them.) Brewers mash and steep grain in hot water, which converts all that starch into sugars. This is traditionally the stage where hops are added to the liquid extract (wort) and boiled to give the beer that hint of bitterness. During the boiling process, a portion of the resins (alpha acids) in hops isomerize into iso-alpha acids. That chemical rearrangement of the molecules is what produces bitterness. Yeast is then added to trigger fermentation, turning the sugars into alcohol.

In a recent development, far from being the chemically inert ingredient brewers have long assumed, hops contain starch enzymes that, under certain conditions, can boost their activity to such a great extent that excessive re-fermentation occurs (“hop-creep”) after bottling. Dry-hopped beers produce significantly higher CO2 levels and packaging pressures, because there is much more re-fermentation going on than usual. And sometimes that pressure builds until the bottle explodes.

Sources indicate that in the wake of the 2020 wildfires, Shellhammer turned his attention to smoke-tainted hops. The primary culprit is volatile phenols (VP), which are produced when the lignin in plant cells is exposed to the high heat of a wildfire. Earlier this year, the OSU team discovered that smoke exposure while the hops are drying increased VP uptake and substantially altered the hops’ aroma; those with higher levels took on meaty, smoky, and artificial BBQ notes; medicinal flavors have also been reported. Those notes were so strong that they overpowered more desirable beery qualities, like citrus notes or aroma intensity.

For this latest project, Shellhammer worked with graduate student Cade Jobe to harvest Idaho-grown Cascade hops. Then they “smoked” the hops in kilns using wood pellets injected into the air intake systems, then dried them. They also harvested and dried non-smoked hops as a control.

Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University.

Sources indicate that next, Shellhammer and Jobe brewed several batches of beer, blending smoke-tainted hops with untainted hops at different levels (25,  50, and 75 percent), along with beer brewed using only tainted hops and beer brewed with no tainted hops. They did this using both a dry-hopping process and one where they added hops during wort boiling. They measured the VP concentrations of each batch of beer with gas chromatography. Finally, a panel of 24 blind tasters evaluated each beer.

Shellhammer and Jobe found that dry-hopping with smoke-tainted hops resulted in increased VP concentrations; the more tainted hops were included, the higher those concentrations. The tasters reported more intense smoky aromas in those beers as well as meaty, smoky, medicinal, and artificial BBQ flavors.

By contrast, when tainted hops were added during the boil, the resulting beer was pretty much indistinguishable from beers brewed with no smoke-tainted hops, even though the former still showed the same increases in VP concentrations. There was no discernible difference when hops were added during the wort boiling stage.

The authors suggest brewers could blend smoke-tainted hops with untainted batches when dry-hopping, keeping the smoke-tainted hops to less than 50 percent. This would still allow brewers to use tainted batches of hops, reducing the economic impact of wildfires on beer production.

Recent findings suggest that “Hop growers and brewers are looking for guidance on whether and how to use smoke-affected hops,” said Jobe. “This research begins to provide some practical information to help hop growers and brewers understand how smoky hops impact beer so that they can make the best decisions.”.

According to recent reports, there’s still more research to be done to confirm the precise ratios and to replicate these initial findings. Future research should also explore the impact of hops exposed to smoke under field conditions, when the plant is still metabolically active, along with consumer studies to evaluate whether beer drinkers more generally will find the flavors of beers made with blended hops (tainted and untainted) acceptable. The findings may not extend to wine production, however, since the fermentation processes are so different, per the authors. And grapes comprise almost all the raw materials in wine, while hops are a smaller fraction of beer brewing ingredients.

Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists, 2026. DOI: 10.1080/03610470.2026.2749166  (About DOIs).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The music streaming platform estimates that it will delete 29 million songs as a result of the AI ban.

The music streaming platform estimates that it will delete 29 million songs as a result of the AI ban.

Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.

It has been revealed that the move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated. In a post on X, Andersen says Tidal needed to take a more “drastic” measure, as AI music made up 43 percent of the tracks distributed to the platform in the last 90 days. “We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all,” Andersen adds.

Industry observers note that bandcamp similarly banned AI music earlier this year, while other music streaming platforms attempt to address a flood of AI songs by applying latest labels or removing them from user algorithms. Spotify recently revealed that it removed 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from recommendations over the past year, and also debuted new “AI persona” badges for artists that use an AI identity. YouTube has rolled out AI music labels as well, while Apple Music is planning to launch AI labels this year. Meanwhile, Deezer is giving people the option to filter out AI music.

“Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale: It diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans,” Tidal notes in a separate post on X.

It has been revealed that the platform is also going to ban music distributors from submitting AI songs, using the AI detection tool Ircam Amplify and metadata checks to reject submissions generated solely with AI. Tidal notes that it won’t ban songs made with the assistance of AI tools, as long as AI doesn’t make up the “sole output.”.

#81559. Tidal is banning AI-generated music entirely

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tidal is banning AI-generated music entirely

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (463 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that tidal will soon become the first streaming service to take a decisive stance against AI-generated music.
  • The move comes after Tidal revealed earlier this year it would demonetize all fully AI-generated track, and label every such song as either AI-generated or AI-assisted.
  • A few months ago, @Tidal tagged and demonetized all wholly AI-generated tracks to protect the authenticity of real artists.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The company expects to purge 29 million tracks.

Sources indicate that tidal will soon become the first streaming service to take a decisive stance against AI-generated music. On Tuesday, the manufacturer announced it would begin removing wholly genAI tracks from its catalog come December 9. According to platform lead Robert Anderson, Tidal's decision will result in the deletion of approximately 29 million tracks, and set the service on the path to reject 80,000 to 85,000 songs daily. "We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96 percent of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all," Anderson wrote on X. "We are the first DSP to do so, and we encourage our peers to follow suit.".

The move comes after Tidal revealed earlier this year it would demonetize all fully AI-generated track, and label every such song as either AI-generated or AI-assisted. On Tuesday, however, Anderson stated even that policy hasn't been enough to combat the deluge of AI tracks that has been flooding Tidal in recent months. Over the last 90 days, 43 percent of all tracks uploaded to the service were flagged as AI-generated, according to the manufacturer.

A few months ago, @Tidal tagged and demonetized all wholly AI-generated tracks to protect the authenticity of real artists. But that's enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done...

According to recent reports, that Tidal should be the first streaming service to ban AI content is somewhat surprising. Block, the organization that has owned Tidal since 2021, is led by AI enthusiast Jack Dorsey. At the start of the year, Block made headlines when it laid off 4,000 of its 10,000 employees, with Dorsey attributing the decision entirely to AI. "The core thesis is simple. Intelligence tools have changed what it means to build and run a company," he wrote at the time. "A significantly smaller team, using the tools we're building, can do more and do it better.".

It has been revealed that the only other streaming platform besides Tidal to outright ban music "generated wholly or in substantial part by AI" is Bandcamp. Spotify, for instance, has tried to dance around the glitch; in October, the organization remarked it would continue to remove "slop and spam" from people's recommendations, but it did this shortly after announcing it would also allow people to remix and cover songs using AI. Soundcloud got into bed with AI music creation companies Elevenlabs and Moises; its current policies try to balance the removal of spam with allowing AI tools to proliferate. Deezer added a toggle to hide (but not delete) AI-made music, while Apple Music merely labels songs made with AI.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A comeback for the ages: Trump's influence on Huang's return to Nvidia.

Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.

Industry observers note that most people are pleased to see the return of the influential billionaire, who declared that he loved China, before videos appeared online of him eating noodles and drinking milk tea during a visit in May. Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets.

But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.

That's probably how Xi Jinping sees it too.

Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt".

Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.

Trunmp and Xi ahead of their meeting in Shenzhen last week.

Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points.

For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington.

In a recent development, trump has said the two men discussed Huang, but did not elaborate further. Beijing has not commented.

The episode has also reinforced the view among Chinese officials that there are two camps in Washington: those in favour of restricting Chinese access to cutting edge tech to protect US national security, and those, like Huang, who believe that such restrictions will not limit Beijing's ambitions.

Huang has repeatedly argued that US export controls will force Chinese firms like Huawei to build independent alternatives - all the while shutting American companies out of the world's second-largest economy.

But him being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

Rather, the sale of advanced chips will remain a key point of contention between the US and China, especially as the two sides try to reach a trade deal before another Trump-Xi meeting, which is expected in December.

Already new rules are being put in place that will worry Beijing.

The US Bureau of Industry and Security is tightening restrictions by targeting not only the direct export of advanced chips to China, but also Chinese firms' ability to use computing power in data centres overseas.

The measures are designed to close potential loopholes that allow Chinese companies to access advanced Nvidia and AMD chips through cloud providers operating in third countries, including Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand.

China has yet to react with measures of its own. But investors will be watching closely for any escalation which could weigh on US equity markets.

Jensen Huang at an Nvidia event in Berlin in October.

And having seen how eager Trump is to keep things stable, Xi may see this as leverage.

In a recent development, he now knows Trump is so worried about the stock market that he is prepared to intervene in the HR decisions of the world's biggest organization. The president has also personally invested in Nvidia, although the White House has emphasised that Trump has placed his businesses in a trust managed by his sons.

China has already used its considerable chokehold over the world's rare earth metals to bring the US to the negotiating table over trade.

If Washington restricts chip exports and Beijing retaliates, that could be the start of a cycle that has a profound effect on the stock market because American companies, from car makers to defence firms to chip manufacturers, all rely on rare earths.

What China has realised is that more trouble lies ahead as it tries to build what it describes as a "constructive strategic relationship" with the US.

In a recent development, trump's tariffs are no longer at the heart of that tussle. Now it's about control of critical technology and minerals which could, in turn, affect each side's military influence and economic power.

What happens next will depend on how the Jensen Huang saga unfolds because it is far from over.

Huang is set to testify before Congress next month, and come January, a Democrat-controlled Congress will raise the pressure. Even some Republican lawmakers have made clear they want answers.

Arkansas senator Tom Cotton wrote on X that the Nvidia controversy "is just the tip of the iceberg and it's not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back".

Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harbinger has tapped Palmer Luckey’s Erebor Bank as a newly introduced source of capital as the electric truck startup looks to diversify how it funds its growth and an expanding portfolio of products spanning autonomous vehicles, energy storage, and defense.

Los Angeles-based Harbinger said Tuesday it secured more than $100 million in financing, including a convertible note from Pinegrove Venture Partners and senior debt from Erebor Bank, which launched in February 2026 and recently surpassed $1 billion in loans, according to the Financial Times.

Industry observers note that the new financing comes less than three weeks after Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D funding round co-led by Tiger Global, Capricorn’s Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. FedEx, which ordered 2,000 trucks from Harbinger, also participated.

It has been revealed that harbinger co-founder and chief executive John Harris explained in a statement that building an industrial technology organization at scale requires a “different financing approach,” adding that the capital needed to ramp up production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn’t have to come entirely from equity. Harris noted that major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations.

Erebor is now Harbinger’s primary banking partner. In a statement, Luckey noted traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and creating U.S. jobs.

“Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology,” he remarked.

Breaking: Ways you can help your video doorbell stay charged in the winter

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Winter can be tough on battery-powered video doorbells, but a few adjustments may help yours cope when temperatures drop.
  • While video doorbells aren't a necessity per se, it can be hard to imagine living without them once you own one.
  • Sources indicate that another catch is that they're perpetually outdoors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winter can be tough on battery-powered video doorbells, but a few adjustments may help yours cope when temperatures drop.

While video doorbells aren't a necessity per se, it can be hard to imagine living without them once you own one. Knowing who's at the door saves you run-ins with unwanted salesmen. More seriously, they may help deter burglars — or help you catch an offender in the act if deterrence fails. Of course, your ability to capture that activity will depend in part on the distance at which your video doorbell stops detecting motion.

Sources indicate that another catch is that they're perpetually outdoors. That might not be such a major deal if you live somewhere warm like Miami or San Antonio. But in places with prolonged cold weather, battery life can suffer to the point that a video doorbell becomes more of a burden than an aid. It's inherent to the chemistry of lithium-ion technology, unfortunately.

The main way to alleviate this matter is by bringing your doorbell or its battery in from the cold. There may be other tactics you can employ, though, such as strategic positioning.

In a recent development, the critical point here is that an ideal charging range for lithium-ion batteries is between 50 and 86 degrees Fahrenheit (10 to 30 Celsius). When charging below the freezing point, there's a risk that metallic lithium will start plating onto electrodes, permanently reducing capacity. And even if the weather is slightly above freezing, charging will be less efficient than it could be. Cold-weather performance is one of the differences between sodium and lithium-ion batteries.

It has been revealed that before you charge a doorbell battery, make sure to let it warm up to room temperature first. This should not only preserve capacity but also help avoid cold-related charging delays. That's significant, considering that a Ring battery can take as long as 10 hours to top up. Let the battery charge fully before putting it back outside to maximize the time between recharges. If your doorbell has a removable battery, keeping a charged spare will minimize downtime. Some models in Ring's updated battery-powered doorbell lineup feature quick-release battery packs to make swaps easier.

Sources indicate that some doorbells don't offer removable batteries, however. One example is the battery-powered Google Nest Doorbell. In that case, you'll need to become familiar with removing your doorbell and bringing it indoors. Be sure to time this properly. Since a recharge might take several hours, it's probably wise to charge overnight unless you're worried about security and don't have any other cameras covering the front of your home.

In a recent development, in climates with borderline winters — that is, where the temperature only occasionally dips below freezing — you may be able to extend battery life by aiming or sheltering your doorbell in just the right way. If you can block the wind, for example, or maximize sunlight, your doorbell will naturally run warmer than it might otherwise.

A vital point here is that in extreme cold, it's possible for a doorbell to stop functioning for the duration. Anker, Ring, Google and others all agree on a minimum operating temperature of -4 degrees Fahrenheit (-20 Celsius). Between that and the freezing point, devices may still refuse to charge in order to prevent the plating we mentioned earlier.

Honestly, then, the best choice if you live in a frostbitten region may be to switch to a wired doorbell, as long as you can find one compatible with your home's design. While wired doorbells may still encounter problems around the -4 degrees Fahrenheit mark, they're otherwise immune to the cold, since they draw on the same electricity as the rest of your house.

Amazon discovers Falcon 9 and Ariane 6 can deliver when nobody else can

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network’s build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket.
  • According to recent reports, the launch was an key rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the organization seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA’s Vulcan rocket, Amazon’s primary launch provider.
