Industry News: This underrated Pixel feature is more versatile than you realize

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're not using this feature, you're missing out on a lot of convenience.
  • If you own a Pixel phone, you probably look forward to the upcoming features that pop up after an Android OS upgrade and Pixel Drop.
  • But there's one old, reliable and underrated feature that you may have missed, and it's actually quite versatile and convenient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're not using this feature, you're missing out on a lot of convenience.

If you own a Pixel phone, you probably look forward to the upcoming features that pop up after an Android OS upgrade and Pixel Drop. The latest Android 17 QPR2 and the November 2026 Pixel Drop, for example, upgraded Pixel Search and added cool customizable icon designs, Transit Mode for train commuters, Pixel VIPs real-time location sharing and a new Status bar settings menu for all Pixel 6a and newer phones, plus expanded Gemini Intelligence, Extreme Charging Mode and other features for the Pixel 10 and 11.

But there's one old, reliable and underrated feature that you may have missed, and it's actually quite versatile and convenient. It's called Quick Tap, and it transforms the back of your Pixel phone into a customizable shortcut when you tap it twice. Quick Tap allows you to accomplish common tasks with just one hand and without scrolling through any menus.

The Quick Tap feature is available on all Pixel 4a (5G) and newer phones. To access it and to customize the settings, open the Settings app on your Pixel phone, then tap System > Gestures > Quick Tap to start actions.

From there, you can then choose a built-in action for Quick Tap to perform when you double-tap the back of your phone. All of these actions are pretty convenient, but since Quick Tap only supports one action at a time, you should choose the one you're likely to use most.

You can assign Quick Tap to turn the flashlight on and off even when your phone is locked. Or set the feature to take a screenshot without having to hold the power and volume-down buttons at the same time. Quick Tap can also play or pause music, videos or podcasts using just about any of your favorite streaming apps with just a couple of taps. This is super convenient when you want to watch or listen to content while you're driving, cooking or working out, because you don't need to unlock the phone, navigate the apps and resume your media. Just double-tap the back of your Pixel.

Use Quick Tap to wake up Gemini without having to talk to the phone. Or assign Quick Tap to easily show notifications without having to pull the notification shade down from the top of the screen; Quick Tap pulls it down for you. You can also use the feature to open the multiple app overview screen and switch between recently used apps without navigating. Quick Tap can also launch any app installed on your Pixel phone — you just need to assign which app you use most.

Sources indicate that one thing to consider: Quick Tap works perfectly on a naked Pixel phone. However, if you have a protective case on your phone, you might need to try a few things to get it working as it should. If your Pixel phone case is super thick, finger tapping may not be enough to get it going. Lighter-weight cases, though, should allow you to activate Quick Tap without much effort.

If you're having trouble, there is an option within the Quick Tap settings called Require stronger taps, designed to prevent accidental triggering of an app when you put the phone down or slide it into your pocket. Make sure that's turned off and then test it out. Messing around with where you tap your phone can also help. If you have a magnetic accessory on the back of the phone, keep tapping around until you find the sweet spot. For the foldable Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Pixel 11 Pro Fold phones, you can tap the rear glass panel whether the phone is unfolded or closed to activate Quick Tap.

It has been revealed that quick Tap can be paired with other apps and automation tools to get even more out of the feature. The Tap, Tap app can be used to supplement Quick Tap by providing support for both double-taps and triple-taps, so you can assign more than one action and choose from a wider range of over 50 available actions to assign. You could also connect Quick Tap to a free pop-up menu or folder app so the double-tap triggers a menu of your most-used apps or tools.

In a recent development, your Pixel phone is also loaded with built-in Gestures, which give you another way to access certain tools and features without having to unlock or swipe — or install another app like Tap, Tap. To find these, go to Settings > System > Gestures.

Let's say you want to use your Quick Tap action to toggle the flashlight when you double-tap the phone, but you also want fast access to your camera or Google Wallet. You can do this by customizing your Gestures to open either the camera or Google Wallet by double-pressing the power button. You can also press and hold the power button to summon Gemini. Then there's the Flip to Shhh feature that automatically enables Do Not Disturb when you place your Pixel phone facedown, as well as a shortcut that lets you tap or lift your phone to check the time, notifications and other info.

Industry observers note that between Quick Tap and Gestures, your Pixel phone is versatile enough to let you simply tap or press your way through a bunch of actions to maximize convenience and one-handed operation. That makes day-to-day phone use much more convenient. Assign it to your smart home device app for quick controllability, or have it open Google Wallet to promptly pay when you're at the store, for example. Anyone who uses a phone knows it's a whole lot easier to tap the phone than to unlock it or swipe through apps... especially if you only have one hand available.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.

It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The Upcoming York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.

According to recent reports, during the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.

Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly noted he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.

It has been revealed that huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House stated Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump noted that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.

Sources indicate that even after all this, Huang reportedly mentioned he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”.

Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do.
  • The partnership, declared Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves.
  • Recent findings suggest that the announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.

The partnership, declared Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work.

Recent findings suggest that the announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea.

To get started, people open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart.

Walmart notes it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent.

Plus, the firm notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.

The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a fresh system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store.

In a recent development, walmart is not the only manufacturer teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant.

Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky.

Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up.

Tech Report: European court finds states can turn back migrants in some cases

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (420 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Court of Human Rights on Tuesday ruled that states belonging to the Council of Europe group have a right to control foreign arrivals.
  • But the court ruling said all 46 member states of the group — that includes all EU and some non-EU countries and promotes democracy and human rights on the continent — must ensure and uphold human rights of people even in hostile environments.
  • The European court ruling is a complicated one since it deals with a case concerning the entry of nationals of Afghanistan, Iraq and Cuba into EU member countries Poland, Latvia and Lithuania between 2021 and 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Court of Human Rights on Tuesday ruled that states belonging to the Council of Europe group have a right to control foreign arrivals.

But the court ruling said all 46 member states of the group — that includes all EU and some non-EU countries and promotes democracy and human rights on the continent — must ensure and uphold human rights of people even in hostile environments.

The European court ruling is a complicated one since it deals with a case concerning the entry of nationals of Afghanistan, Iraq and Cuba into EU member countries Poland, Latvia and Lithuania between 2021 and 2022.

That was a time when a border standoff was playing out between Belarus and the EU's eastern member states, with Belarus having been accused of entirely manufacturing a migration crisis to put pressure on the EU.

Belarus arranged for people from various third countries to enter their state and then pointed them to the EU's frontiers.

Europe's most vital human rights court on Tuesday ruled that states have a right to control the entry of foreign nationals into their territory even when migration has been weaponized.

The court calls Belarus' hostile actions of 2021 as having been an instance of "instrumentalization of migration.".

But the court said that states must still ensure that migrants are protected against inhumane or degrading treatment.

In the context of a surge in migration, for example, national authorities were still to identify people who were particularly at risk of suffering or enduring ill treatment.

The migrants in the case brought before the European court remarked that they had been violently prevented from crossing into the EU without their asylum applications having been examined and that their human rights had been violated.

"In a context of instrumentalization of migration, the removal of a foreign national to the instrumentalizing state would not, as such, constitute a violation of Article 3 (prohibition of torture and inhuman and degrading treatment)," the court press release said.

The court ordered Poland, Latvia and Lithuania to pay compensation for their treatment of migrants at the EU's external borders with Belarus.

Five EU countries also last week declared a plan with Rwanda to establish a so-called return hub in the African nation.

The hub will host rejected asylum seekers waiting to return to their countries of origin.

#81498. What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?

What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1158 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis.
  • It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it.
  • The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset.

It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math.

The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, “It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most vital problems in the field.”.

The proof of the hypothesis was unveiled by a mathematician named Levent Alpöge, who has been working at Anthropic, and, not surprisingly, used Claude to generate it. His announcement is written in a somewhat florid style (example: “one of which was already new and shocking, making very simple one of the shadows of Riemann over which we mathematicians felt most triumph”), and he has apparently dropped some hints that some of it was meant in jest.

According to recent reports, but it does make clear that this proof was a longstanding interest of Alpöge’s, and he had some insights into how to connect different areas of math to reach the final proof. The process seems to have involved getting the AI started with handling a simplified “toy” form of some of Alpöge’s insights and then directing it to expand what it found there to the full scope of the Riemann hypothesis.

Sources indicate that the proof itself comes in two different forms, and the difference between them gets at the heart of why AI usage in math has been controversial. One is a rigorous description of the proof using a programming language named Lean that has allowed the rapid verification that the proof is valid. The second is a description of the logic behind it, which may ultimately be the key for mathematics as a field to benefit from this proof.

It’s important to emphasize that, so far at least, AI has been solving problems that humans previously recognized as significant. That significance is typically ascribed to mathematical ideas because of their implications or utility—they either tell us something about areas of math that people care about, or they keep popping up in problems that mathematicians are working on. So far, there are no indications that AI can recognize or formulate interesting and important unresolved problems on its own.

Recent findings suggest that but AI has tackled many problems humans have considered significant with impressive ease. Trained on a body of material that included a lot of advanced math, the software has provided both formal proofs as well as counterexamples that have clearly demonstrated that some proposals are incorrect.

When it comes to proofs, AI might have some advantages over people. For starters, it’s not specialized in specific fields of math and can potentially pull together tools from a variety of disciplines. AI also pays no cost (either in terms of career or emotional soundness) from going down the wrong track, giving up, and starting over.

AI models have also had one of their biggest limitations removed via humanity’s development of Lean, a computer language that allows mathematical proofs to be expressed in a way that can be readily verified. Due to their tendency to hallucinate, a description of a proof generated by an AI would still require extensive human validation before it could be accepted, a task that might radically shift the effort/reward ratio of using AI models. But by instructing an AI to include the necessary Lean code as part of its output, verification has become straightforward.

The unfortunate aspect of this for mathematics as a field is that it’s often the process of working through the reasoning behind a proof, rather than the step-by-step logic, that advances the field as a whole.

Mathematicians have expressed their fears about this aspect of AI usage in a formal open letter. We’ll try to connect those fears to the recent announcement.

Sources indicate that before AI, proofs were typically worked through by people who recognized potential pathways connecting disparate fields of math and spent years finding ways to formalize those intuitions and validate that the math worked. It wasn’t necessarily an efficient use of time if the only output was the proof itself.

Sources indicate that but that was rarely the case. By finding the connections between problems, this work helped many other people see new ways of tackling whatever issues they were wrestling with. Mathematicians often developed new tools, found shortcuts, or stumbled across related problems while working through their proofs, enriching math as a whole. In other words, the proof itself was often less important for math than the process of generating it.

According to recent reports, by contrast, the internal workings of large neural networks are notoriously opaque. Asking an AI to explain its reasoning runs into the same problems that asking it anything else does: Since the software has only been selected for producing decent-sounding text, it’s likely to make something up that sounds good when asked about its own internal processes. So, an AI-generated proof has little to offer the field in terms of new ideas or unexpected advances, at least on its own.

Recent findings suggest that indeed, nobody can say much about the Riemann proof at the moment, simply because mathematicians have barely started the process of shifting through the logic as expressed in Lean. It’s possible it can eventually produce newly introduced insights and tools, but it may take years before humans can figure out what they are and how to express them in a way that other mathematicians can appreciate.

How mathematicians are expected to identify fresh challenges that can push their fields beyond the current body while seeing AI relieve them of the need to actually do math is anybody’s guess.

This is all new and progressing incredibly swiftly; there has been no time for the field to find a new normal. It’s possible that, once Alpöge gets around to describing the approach he pushed Claude to use, mathematicians will start getting the same sorts of insights that they normally expect to receive from proofs. It could be that Alpöge’s approach, mixing human intuition with machine-generated detail and rigor, provides a model for what math will look like in a few years.

But it’s impossible to tell at this early stage in development.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: India's government is 'scared', cockroach movement leader says after travel ban.

One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has stated the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.

Saurav Das mentioned he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.

In an interview with the BBC, Das remarked there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people.

The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident highlighted the government was "scared".

In a recent development, "They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them.".

By not allowing him to travel, he remarked the government had lowered India's stature in the world.

Industry observers note that "It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he mentioned. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light.

"It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government.".

Das said he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement.

Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country.".

On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".

Saurav Das (L) speaking following the resignation of India's education minister in July.

Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.

In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .

In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.

The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

Das insisted the CJP would continue protesting, but it did not want to be a political party "as of today".

"It's a long haul. We are not here for a short time. We are looking at India in the next 10 to 20 years. How do we develop India into a better country? That is the vision that we want to carry forward.".

Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.

There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.

In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.

In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

Additional reporting by Cherylann Mollan.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (886 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants.
  • In a recent development, according to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time.
  • ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But upcoming research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.

In a recent development, according to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.

ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.

The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.

In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.

Sources indicate that shellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.

Industry observers note that it seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest-performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.

For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another task, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.

The findings highlight a major issue for customers adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.

While AI benchmarks have largely focused on coding, professional work, or testing on specific tasks, ShellBench is attempting to evaluate how models perform on multi-step personal tasks within different agent harnesses — the software that controls how a model accesses information, uses tools, and takes actions.

While the researchers found model choice had a greater overall impact on performance than harness choice, among the more capable models, AI agent performance became more dependent on the harness.

For example, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 when operating within the Pi harness, but it performed worse when both models were tested within Claude Code.

Meta’s Muse Wonder Full scored 56% in Pi, but only 38.1% in Claude Code. Meta’s Muse Wonder 1.0, meanwhile, averaged a success rate of 39.7% across the five harnesses tested.

Notably, while the researchers tested models from Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic, they didn’t evaluate them within the native harnesses of Muse, Dots, or Claude Duet, so the results may not be representative of the experience millions of consumers are having with the product today.

TechCrunch has reached out to Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and the researchers in the study.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.

The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.

Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.

Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations.

In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence â of which six months were suspended â over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign.

Sources indicate that in 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail â two of them suspended â and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail.

The latest case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had mentioned he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the â¬50m (Â£43m) in payments continued after he became president.

Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020.

At the time, Sarkozy was said to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a newly introduced investigation was launched into the "Save Sarko" file â the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media.

So the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" and benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEO.
  • US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.
  • Blanche mentioned he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEO.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.

Blanche mentioned he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.

Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about.".

Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.

The US commerce department has also declared it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China.

In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments remarked they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".

But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche said the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time.

"So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the company or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche noted: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.

"Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.

"It shouldn't be what my message would be either.".

While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.

The company's share price closed down nearly 6% - still well above where it ended last week. On Monday, Nvidia stock rocketed more than 31% following news of Huang's return.

Faisal Islam: Fears over the AI boom haven't gone away.

The tech giant's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, mentioned Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

The board mentioned it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.

On Monday, Trump said he spoke to the tech giant's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.

Huang's reinstatement provoked bipartisan anger.

Republican congressman Don Bacon said Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".

Republican Senator Pete Ricketts noted Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".

Democratic congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".

Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego remarked Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".

    According to recent reports, given everything moms do for us, it feels good to give back during the holidays. But where to start? How do you come up with a physical representation of how you feel about such a key and influential figure in your life? The possibilities seem as endless as they are daunting, but fear not, we’ve done the hard work for you.

    Industry observers note that to help you make the mother figure in your life feel truly appreciated, we’ve created a sprawling list of intriguing, lovingly curated gift ideas. From a ring watch and luxe portable gaming deck to a better robovac and an AI-powered bird feeder that brings nature to her doorstep, our list has something to fit all of your mom’s many facets, at a wide range of price points. So take one more thing off your checklist and get her something she’ll truly adore this year.

    Industry observers note that CDs are back, and it’s not just about the fantastic sound quality. Like vinyl, part of the appeal is the tactile nature of an album on disc. km5’s Cp1 accentuates the vibe with a minimalist form factor that lets you place the jacket art above the disc, plus modern extras like a rechargeable battery and Bluetooth.

    According to recent reports, built for jet setters, Anker’s 100W travel adapter features a durable design, a handy LCD display to track charge percentage, and compatibility in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does have four USB inputs for all your portables, including a trio of USB-C ports.

    If you’re contemplating a pricey pair of sleep buds for your loved one, we urge you to halt and consider a softer (and cheaper) alternative. Piercing pillows, designed with pockets for freshly pierced ears, also work great for regular earbuds. Blissbury’s comfy and adjustable Ear Pillow is our favorite. Problem — and sleep problems — solved.

    SwitchBot’s futuristic block, which is designed to activate physical switches from afar, is as useful as it is eccentric. Also available in a rechargeable configuration, the app-controllable button pusher clips onto almost anything with a switch and lasts up to 600 days on a single 3V CR2 battery.

    The BYOK (Bring Your Own Keyboard) is a distraction-free way for creatives to get their thoughts down without the allure of silly YouTube videos or notifications about their dog’s flea meds. No frills, just a low-resolution LCD screen that works with most keyboards and provides plenty of power for the long haul.

    If you want to gift your mom something completely different, Bandai’s silly Cup Noodle model offers accurate 3D-scanned details, right down to the egg, shrimp, and “mystery meat.” It’s sure to surprise and delight any hobbyist, especially those with a sense of whimsy.

    For the coffee- or tea-loving mom in your life who’s always headed to the microwave for a heat zap, Ember’s fancy-schmancy smart mug is a luxurious way to keep things toasty. With the ability to set the temperature on the mug or in the app, the Mug 3 makes it simple to keep liquids perfectly hot indefinitely.

    Govee’s latest lamppost is a nifty gift for any mom looking to light up the yard without invasive procedures. The water-resistant lamp offers 360-degree lighting with adjustable colors at up to 2,000 lumens, built-in motion sensors, a long power cord, and Matter compatibility for versatile smart control.

    In a recent development, for any mom after a travel-friendly hair dryer, the Laifen Mini is a must. Affordable, attractive, and powerful, it puts out up to 110,000RPM of drying power in a packable design that weighs well under a pound.

    According to recent reports, for the mother, father, or other dedicated organizer in your life, enter the P-Touch Cube. The modern label maker offers simple operation and compatibility with iOS and Android, letting consumers design and personalize custom labels and ribbons on their phones for a fun way to put a label on it.

    Recent findings suggest that soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for way less than Apple’s latest AirPods Pro.

    Industry observers note that aura’s aptly titled feeder places its camera beside the feeder instead of inside it, giving you a wider view of nature’s modern dinos. With 2.5K resolution, built-in solar panels, and AI bird identification (all without a pricey subscription), it’s the modern way to bird.

    In a recent development, for on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote.

    Sources indicate that if a Kindle won’t quite fit into your favorite traveler’s tight pack job, consider the Xteink X4 Pro. The tiny e-reader is easy to pop into your bag or pocket thanks to its 4.3-inch display, and the latest model offers a backlit touchscreen for a more intuitive way to explore the literary world.

    Sources indicate that hoto’s soldering iron is super cool — and by that we mean hot, as it’s able to reach nearly 400 degrees Fahrenheit in about three seconds. The cordless, adjustable iron makes the perfect gift for your favorite DIYer, especially since it features customizable presets for virtually any job.

    The future is now, so of course we’ve got screens in sunglasses. The Viture Pro 2 are a slick pair of augmented-reality shades with speakers, micro-OLED screens, and a bonus feature: diopter-adjusting dials, which can sharpen the focus of whatever they’re mirroring from a phone or other device over a USB-C tether. Fancy!

    We love JisuLife’s basic but effective cooling fan, which offers simple operation, five speeds, and an LCD battery display. Sure, you could spend a hundred bucks or more on a personal cooler, but the rechargeable 10 S is a stellar — and relatively compact — way to beat the heat on a budget.

    Industry observers note that we’re not used to talking about “budget” Apple products, but the multicolored MacBook Neo isn’t your average Apple device. The stripped-down MacBook packs enough firepower for everyday tasks, along with a pleasing screen and a terrific mechanical trackpad, giving Mom everything she needs at a manageable price.

    According to recent reports, it’s time for a smarter robovac. Thankfully, there’s the Matic, which looks less like the rambling discs that pervade the space and more like an actual robot that, well, vacuums. It doesn’t get under beds, but it also doesn’t get stuck under them, and it does a great job providing truly no-fuss cleaning thanks to its superb mapping.

    It has been revealed that if you haven’t been bombarded by the Hulken yet, it’s a rolling tote that’s blown up online. Designed to hold everything from laundry to an impromptu picnic, the durable bag is beloved for its seemingly bottomless capacity and colorful style, making it a thoughtful gift for fashionable moms on the move.

    There’s no shortage of mobile gaming controllers, but few are as stealthy or as compact as the MCON. The sliding gamepad rapidly attaches to any MagSafe- or Pixelsnap-ready phone, letting you game with a set of satisfying controls that feel more natural than most rivals.

    According to recent reports, so what if you’ve heard “Golden” more times than you can count? Netflix’s massive animated hit is a lot easier to gift now that it’s officially available on 4K Blu-ray disc. The story about three pop stars who band together to save humanity from a demonic boy band is an instant classic, with fantastic music and striking animation.

    Sources indicate that the HoverAir X1 is the hands-off drone your mom didn’t know she needed. Marketed as a “selfie drone,” the autonomous X1 is super light, fits in a small bag, and includes five predetermined flight paths for snapping photos based on your location, with a sixth pattern you can customize.

    Digital photos changed everything, but there’s still something wonderful about the visceral touch and nostalgia of analog.     Industry observers note that give the gift of prolonged hearing (and brain health) with these fashionable yet functional earplugs from Loop.     In a recent development, mom works hard, and she deserves some self-care. Even if you can’t send her to a spa, you can bring a bit of luxury home with CeraVe’s fragrance-free eye cream, which is designed to reduce dark circles and remove unwanted puffiness.

    Recent findings suggest that dock & Bay’s blankets are well suited for the latest parents in your circle.     Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.

    Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.

    According to recent reports, game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one massive effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.

    Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.

    PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.

    At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

    In a recent development, coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

    • After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.
    • Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday.
    • It has been revealed that the founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

    Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”.

    It has been revealed that the founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest organization meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.

    “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

    The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”.

    Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also stated that he was grateful for a second chance at the tech giant.

    It has been revealed that the CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The President reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role.

    Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he mentioned helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low,” the Wall Street Journal writes.

    Sources indicate that huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of Congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

    Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa.

    Recent findings suggest that when the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

    It has been revealed that “Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”.
